title: David Stockman: Buy Gold Before The Financial System Unravels
speaker: David Stockman

macro_themes.view: Public debt at $40T is on a path to $150-200T by mid-century under realistic rates; unsustainable, something breaks first.
Kevin Warsh is a 'junior Volcker' who won't restart QE or bail out markets, so yields must be set by real supply and demand.
Interest rates have been rising for 12-18 months and will go considerably higher, grinding the economy down and possibly causing recession.
Market at 22-25x earnings; nine leading AI stocks at ~130x free cash flow; tens of trillions of market cap could be wiped out without a Fed bailout.
Hot wholesale prices (PPI ~15% annualised in September) leave the Fed no room to ease.
Dollar won't crash on an FX basis because EU, China and Japan are worse off.
Revaluing Fort Knox gold means nothing; small gold-backed bond issuance would be symbolic only.

calls.reason: Unsustainable debt, rising rates and an end to Fed bailouts; gold is 'only going to go up', he won't say when or how fast.
calls.quote: I'm a gold bug, okay? So I think people should load up on that. There it's it's only going to go up.

calls.reason: Market absurdly overvalued at 22-25x earnings with rampant speculation; a hawkish Fed that won't bail out plus rising rates will end the party.
calls.quote: the financial markets now are very dangerous places. The stock market is absurdly overvalued.

calls.instrument_quoted: nine largest AI stocks (Google, Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon etc.)
calls.reason: Leading AI stocks went from $4T to $24T market cap while free cash flow grew ~2%/yr, now ~130x FCF; halving the multiple erases ~$12T.
calls.quote: There's nothing in the known universe or the unknown universe that's worth 130 times free cash flow.

calls.reason: With no Fed bond buying, $2-3T/yr of deficits plus rollovers must be financed by real savings, so yields go considerably higher; prefers T-bills over 30-year bonds.
calls.quote: I think they're going considerably higher and what that will do is grind the economy down to to a crawl at best

calls.reason: Dollar is the cleanest dirty shirt; EU, China and Japan are in worse shape, so no FX crash despite US debt.
calls.quote: on a pure exchange rate basis, I don't think the dollar is going down.

notes: TYX price_at_call 5.3 from '30-year bonds... yielding 5.3 or 5.5, whatever the number is' (approximate). Bias on yields is for yields up (bearish bonds). DXY coded neutral: he says it won't go down but gives no upside view. 'Yesterday' hot PPI implies a date near a September PPI release, but no explicit date, so listing date used. Contains conference promo.
